slides.headline: Build an emergency fund
slides.body: The 4-stage plan nobody spells out

slides.headline: 1. Start with ₹10,000
slides.body: Not 6 months of expenses. Just ₹10k first. A reachable number you'll actually hit.

slides.headline: 2. Get to one month
slides.body: One month of expenses covers most real emergencies. This is where panic-borrowing stops.

slides.headline: 3. Park it in a liquid fund
slides.body: Not the savings account you spend from. Separate + slightly harder to reach = it survives.

slides.headline: 4. Then aim for 3-6 months
slides.body: Only now. Building the full cushion before step 1 is why most people never start.

slides.headline: Read your payslip properly
slides.body: 4 lines that actually matter

slides.headline: 1. Gross vs net
slides.body: Gross is the headline. Net is what lands. The gap is where everything below hides.

slides.headline: 2. Your PF contribution
slides.body: Deducted, but it's yours — forced savings earning ~8%. Not a loss, a hidden asset.

slides.headline: 3. The tax slab you're in
slides.body: Know it before it's deducted. It decides whether old or new regime saves you more.

slides.headline: 4. Reimbursements vs allowances
slides.body: Allowances are taxed. Reimbursements often aren't. Structuring these cuts your tax.

slides.headline: Stock your first kitchen
slides.body: 5 basics that cook almost anything

slides.headline: 1. One good knife
slides.body: A single sharp chef's knife beats a block of dull ones. The tool you'll use daily.

slides.headline: 2. A heavy-bottomed pan
slides.body: Even heat, nothing burns. One pan for eggs, sabzi, and searing — buy quality once.

slides.headline: 3. Salt, oil, acid, heat
slides.body: Every dish needs these four. Master balancing them before buying 20 spices.

slides.headline: 4. Rice + dal + eggs
slides.body: The trinity. A dozen cheap, fast meals live inside just these three.

slides.headline: Over-salted your food?
slides.body: 4 fixes before you toss it

slides.headline: 1. Add a raw potato
slides.body: Drop chunks into the simmering dish. They absorb salt. Remove before serving.

slides.headline: 2. Bulk it up
slides.body: More water, more veg, more base. Dilutes the salt across a bigger volume.

slides.headline: 3. Add acid or sugar
slides.body: A squeeze of lemon or pinch of sugar rebalances the taste and masks saltiness.

slides.headline: 4. Serve with something plain
slides.body: Rice, bread, or yogurt on the side pulls the perceived saltiness right down.

slides.headline: Guests in 20 minutes?

slides.headline: 1. Clear flat surfaces
slides.body: Counters, table, coffee table. Clutter reads as 'dirty' more than actual dirt does.

slides.headline: 2. The bathroom sink + mirror

slides.headline: 3. Dim the lights
slides.body: Softer light hides dust instantly. Lamps over harsh overheads. Instant 'clean enough'.

slides.headline: 4. One good smell

slides.headline: Just stained your shirt?
slides.body: The first 60 seconds decide everything

slides.headline: 1. Blot, never rub
slides.body: Rubbing drives the stain into the fibres. Press and lift with a clean cloth instead.

slides.headline: 2. Cold water for most
slides.body: Hot water sets protein stains (blood, egg, sweat). Cold first, always, when unsure.

slides.headline: 3. Grease needs dish soap
slides.body: Oil stains laugh at detergent. A drop of dish soap cuts grease before the wash.

slides.headline: 4. Never dry until it's gone
slides.body: The dryer bakes a stain in permanently. Air-dry and re-treat until it's fully out.

slides.headline: Surviving a long-haul flight
slides.body: 4 things that actually work

slides.headline: 1. Aisle for long, window for red-eyes
slides.body: Aisle = move freely. Window = a wall to sleep against. Pick by trip type, not habit.

slides.headline: 2. Hydrate before you board
slides.body: Cabin air is desert-dry. Drink on the ground; you'll ask for less bad coffee up there.

slides.headline: 3. Set your watch to arrival time
slides.body: The moment you board. Your brain starts adjusting to the new zone before you land.

slides.headline: 4. Walk every 3 hours
slides.body: Not just comfort — it cuts the real clot risk of sitting still for 10+ hours.

slides.headline: Avoid tourist scams
slides.body: The same 4 show up everywhere

slides.headline: 1. The 'free' bracelet or rose
slides.body: Nothing handed to you is free. Once it's on your wrist, they demand payment. Don't accept.

slides.headline: 2. The broken taxi meter
slides.body: 'Meter not working' = inflated fare. Agree the price before the door shuts, or use an app.

slides.headline: 3. The overly helpful stranger
slides.body: At ATMs and ticket machines. 'Helping' is distraction while someone watches your PIN.

slides.headline: 4. The restaurant with no prices
slides.body: No menu prices means the bill is invented for you. Prices on the menu, or walk away.

slides.headline: Just moved in?

slides.headline: 4. Change the locks
slides.body: You don't know who has old keys. First-week job, before you trust the place.

slides.headline: Make a small room feel big

slides.headline: 1. Hang curtains high + wide
slides.body: Rod near the ceiling, wider than the window. The eye reads the whole wall as taller.

slides.headline: 4. One big piece, not many small

slides.headline: Start your first SIP
slides.body: Zero to invested in 4 steps

slides.headline: 1. Finish KYC once
slides.body: Aadhaar + PAN, done digitally in minutes. One-time gate before any fund lets you in.

slides.headline: 2. Pick one index fund
slides.body: A Nifty 50 index fund as your core. Low cost, no fund-manager guesswork. Start there.

slides.headline: 3. Automate the date
slides.body: Set the SIP for 2 days after payday. You invest before you can spend it.

slides.headline: 4. Ignore it for a year
slides.body: Don't check daily. SIPs work through boring consistency, not clever timing.

slides.headline: Fix your credit score
slides.body: 4 levers that actually move it

slides.headline: 1. Pay on time, always
slides.body: Payment history is the biggest factor. One missed EMI hurts more than any single hack helps.

slides.headline: 2. Stay under 30% usage
slides.body: Using ₹30k of a ₹1L limit looks fine. Using ₹90k signals risk, even if you pay it off.

slides.headline: 3. Don't close old cards
slides.body: Age of credit helps you. An old unused card quietly boosts your score just by existing.

slides.headline: 4. Check your report yearly
slides.body: Errors are common and drag your score. One free check a year catches them.

slides.headline: Negotiate your salary
slides.body: 4 moves before you say yes

slides.headline: 1. Never say your number first
slides.body: The first number anchors everything. Ask their range before you reveal yours.

slides.headline: 2. Negotiate the whole package
slides.body: Base is one lever. Joining bonus, notice buyout, WFH days all have room too.

slides.headline: 3. Get the offer in writing first
slides.body: Verbal offers evaporate. Negotiate only once it's on paper and real.

slides.headline: 4. Silence is a tactic
slides.body: State your number, then stop talking. The pause does more work than more words.

slides.headline: Insurance you actually need
slides.body: Skip the rest. These 3 matter.

slides.headline: 1. Term life (if others depend on you)
slides.body: Pure protection, cheap. Covers your family if you're gone. No investment gimmicks attached.

slides.headline: 2. Health cover, separate from work

slides.headline: Never get ambushed by a bill
slides.body: The sinking-fund method, 4 steps

slides.headline: 1. List your once-a-year costs
slides.body: Insurance, school fees, festivals, car service. The big ones that 'surprise' you every year.

slides.headline: 2. Add them up, divide by 12
slides.body: A ₹24k annual bill is ₹2k a month. Now it's a small monthly line, not a yearly shock.

slides.headline: 3. Auto-move it monthly
slides.body: A standing transfer to a separate 'bills' pot. It builds quietly in the background.

slides.headline: 4. Pay from the pot, guilt-free
slides.body: When the bill lands, the money's already there. No scramble, no card debt, no stress.

slides.headline: Beat lifestyle creep
slides.body: When your raise vanishes, this is why

slides.headline: 1. Save the raise, not the salary
slides.body: Next time income jumps, bank the increase first. Live on what you already managed on.

slides.headline: 2. Wait 3 months before upgrading
slides.body: New income makes everything feel affordable. Wait, and half the 'needs' quietly fade.

slides.headline: 3. Track your savings rate, not amount
slides.body: Saving more rupees while earning far more can still mean saving a smaller share. Watch the %.

slides.headline: 4. Upgrade one thing, not everything
slides.body: Pick the upgrade that matters most to you. Let the rest stay boringly the same.

slides.headline: Chop like you mean it
slides.body: 4 habits for faster, safer cutting

slides.headline: 1. The claw grip
slides.body: Curl your fingertips under, knuckles guide the blade. Your fingers physically can't be cut.

slides.headline: 2. Let the knife do the work
slides.body: Stop pressing down hard. A sharp blade glides — you're guiding, not forcing.

slides.headline: 3. Flat side down first
slides.body: Cut a round veg in half, sit it flat, then slice. It can't roll into your fingers.

slides.headline: 4. A damp cloth under the board
slides.body: Stops it sliding. A moving board is where most kitchen cuts actually happen.

slides.headline: Meal prep in one session
slides.body: Cook once, eat all week

slides.headline: 1. Prep components, not meals
slides.body: Cook rice, a protein, and two veg separately. Mix differently each day so it never bores you.

slides.headline: 2. Roast a whole tray at once
slides.body: One oven tray of mixed veg feeds several meals. Hands-off while it cooks.

slides.headline: 3. Store in clear containers
slides.body: You eat what you see. Opaque boxes become science experiments at the back of the fridge.

slides.headline: 4. Freeze half on day one
slides.body: By day 4 you're sick of it. Freeze half fresh so week-old food never happens.

slides.headline: Stop wasting food
slides.body: 4 habits that cut your bin in half

slides.headline: 1. Shop your fridge first
slides.body: Before buying, cook what's already there. Most waste is food bought on top of food.

slides.headline: 2. 'Eat me first' shelf
slides.body: One fridge shelf for things about to turn. Nothing hides and dies at the back.

slides.headline: 3. Freeze before it turns
slides.body: Bread, herbs, cheese, even milk freeze fine. Freeze at the edge, not after it's gone.

slides.headline: 4. Cook stems and scraps
slides.body: Veg peels and stems make stock. Free flavour from what you'd normally throw away.

slides.headline: Better home coffee
slides.body: 4 fixes, no expensive machine

slides.headline: 1. Fresh grind beats everything
slides.body: Pre-ground coffee is stale within days. Grinding just before brewing is the single biggest jump.

slides.headline: 2. Get the water off the boil
slides.body: Boiling water scorches coffee bitter. Wait 30 seconds after boiling before you pour.

slides.headline: 3. Weigh, don't eyeball
slides.body: Roughly 1:15 coffee to water. A cheap scale makes every cup repeatable instead of random.

slides.headline: 4. Clean your equipment
slides.body: Old coffee oils turn every fresh brew rancid. A rinse and monthly deep clean fixes 'bad beans'.

slides.headline: Dish tastes flat?
slides.body: It's almost always one of these 4

slides.headline: 1. It needs acid
slides.body: Lemon, vinegar, tamarind. The most common missing note — it lifts everything else awake.

slides.headline: 2. It needs salt (still)
slides.body: Under-salted food tastes dull, not bland. Add a little, taste, repeat. It's usually this.

slides.headline: 3. It needs fat
slides.body: A knob of butter, a drizzle of oil, some cream. Fat carries flavour and rounds harsh edges.

slides.headline: 4. It needs something roasted
slides.body: Toasted spices, browned onions, a seared edge. Raw-tasting food lacks this deep base note.

slides.headline: Cook for your freezer
slides.body: 4 rules for meals that survive it

slides.headline: 1. Freeze flat in bags
slides.body: Lay bags flat to freeze, then stand them like files. Saves space and thaws in minutes.

slides.headline: 2. Label with the date
slides.body: Everything looks identical frozen. A date and name saves you unwrapping mystery bricks.

slides.headline: 3. Some things hate freezing
slides.body: Potatoes go grainy, cream splits, crisp things go soggy. Freeze curries, soups, and bakes instead.

slides.headline: 4. Cool fully before freezing
slides.body: Warm food raises the freezer temp and part-thaws its neighbours. Cool first, always.

slides.headline: Deep clean your fridge
slides.body: 4 steps, start to finish

slides.headline: 1. Empty and bin first
slides.body: Everything out. Toss the expired and the mystery jars now, before you clean around them.

slides.headline: 2. Shelves out, warm soapy water
slides.body: Never cold — cold glass shelves can crack under hot water. Warm and mild does it.

slides.headline: 3. Wipe with baking soda paste
slides.body: Cuts grease and kills fridge smell at once. No harsh chemicals near your food.

slides.headline: 4. Restock oldest at the front
slides.body: New stuff to the back. You use the front first, so nothing expires forgotten again.

slides.headline: Burnt pan?
slides.body: 4 fixes that beat scrubbing

slides.headline: 1. Boil water in it
slides.body: Add water, bring to a boil, let it loosen the burnt layer. Half the job does itself.

slides.headline: 2. Baking soda + a little water
slides.body: Make a paste, leave 15 minutes. It lifts burnt residue without scratching the surface.

slides.headline: 3. Vinegar for the stubborn bits
slides.body: Simmer water and vinegar, then add baking soda off heat. The fizz breaks the bond.

slides.headline: 4. Never a metal scourer on non-stick
slides.body: It wrecks the coating for good. Soak longer instead — patience beats scratching.

slides.headline: Keep a clean home
slides.body: 4 tiny habits beat one big clean

slides.headline: 1. Never leave a room empty-handed
slides.body: Carry one out-of-place thing with you every time you leave. Tidying that never feels like tidying.

slides.headline: 2. Clean while you wait
slides.body: Kettle boiling? Wipe a counter. Dead minutes become done chores without extra time.

slides.headline: 3. One-touch rule
slides.body: Deal with a thing once — put it away, not 'down for now'. 'For now' is how piles are born.

slides.headline: 4. Reset before bed
slides.body: Five minutes returning things to place. You wake to calm instead of yesterday's mess.

slides.headline: Clean your screens properly
slides.body: 4 rules to not wreck them

slides.headline: 1. Power off first
slides.body: You see smudges clearly on a black screen, and you won't trigger anything mid-wipe.

slides.headline: 2. Microfibre only
slides.body: Paper towel and tissue micro-scratch coatings. A microfibre cloth is the only safe wipe.

slides.headline: 3. Never spray the screen
slides.body: Liquid seeps into ports and edges. Spray the cloth lightly, then wipe — never the device.

slides.headline: 4. Skip alcohol on phones
slides.body: It strips the oil-resistant coating over time. Water on microfibre is enough for daily grime.

slides.headline: Bathroom in 10 minutes
slides.body: The order that gets it done fast

slides.headline: 1. Spray everything first
slides.body: Hit the shower, sink, and toilet with cleaner, then walk away. Let it work while you do the rest.

slides.headline: 2. Clear the clutter
slides.body: Bottles off the counter, towels straightened. A tidy surface reads clean before you've scrubbed.

slides.headline: 3. Wipe top-down
slides.body: Mirror, then sink, then toilet, then floor last. Gravity means you never re-dirty what's done.

slides.headline: 4. Finish with the floor
slides.body: A quick mop or wipe pulls up the hair and dust that fell while you cleaned above.

slides.headline: Kill a bad smell
slides.body: 4 fixes that beat masking it

slides.headline: 1. Find the source, don't spray over it
slides.body: Air freshener on a real smell just makes a worse smell. Hunt the cause first — bin, drain, damp.

slides.headline: 2. Baking soda absorbs, doesn't cover
slides.body: An open bowl in the fridge or a sprinkle on carpet pulls odour out of the air overnight.

slides.headline: 3. Simmer for a fresh kitchen
slides.body: Water with citrus peel and cinnamon on a low simmer fills the home naturally, no chemicals.

slides.headline: 4. Air it out daily
slides.body: Ten minutes of cross-breeze clears stale air better than any spray. Open opposite windows.

slides.headline: Beat jet lag
slides.body: 4 fixes that actually work

slides.headline: 1. Chase daylight on arrival
slides.body: Get outside in the sun at your destination. Light resets your body clock faster than anything.

slides.headline: 2. Eat on the new schedule
slides.body: Meal times are a clock signal too. Eat when locals eat, even if you're not hungry yet.

slides.headline: 3. No long nap on day one
slides.body: A 20-min nap is fine. A 3-hour crash locks in the wrong timezone and drags it out for days.

slides.headline: 4. Flying east is harder
slides.body: Losing hours hits worse than gaining them. Shift your sleep earlier a few days before you go.

slides.headline: Find cheaper flights
slides.body: 4 levers that actually work

slides.headline: 1. Be flexible on dates, not destination
slides.body: The same trip a few days either way can swing hundreds. Use the flexible-date calendar view.

slides.headline: 2. Set a price alert early
slides.body: Track the route weeks out. You learn its normal price, so you recognise a real deal when it drops.

slides.headline: 3. Check nearby airports
slides.body: A second airport an hour away can be far cheaper. Factor the transfer, then compare honestly.

slides.headline: 4. Book connections separately, carefully
slides.body: Two one-way tickets sometimes beat one return — but leave buffer, since it's not one protected trip.

slides.headline: Your first solo trip
slides.body: 4 things that make it easier

slides.headline: 1. Arrive in daylight
slides.body: Book flights that land before dark. A new place is far less daunting when you can see it.

slides.headline: 2. Share your location with one person
slides.body: Live location to someone at home. Freedom to explore, with a quiet safety net running.

slides.headline: 3. Book the first night only
slides.body: Lock in day one so you're not stranded, then stay flexible once you've read the place.

slides.headline: 4. Eat at the bar
slides.body: Solo dining feels awkward at a table, natural at the bar — and that's where you meet people.

slides.headline: Carry-on only, every trip
slides.body: 4 rules to never check a bag

slides.headline: 1. Pick one colour palette
slides.body: Everything mixes and matches. Fewer pieces, more outfits, half the bag — nothing wasted.

slides.headline: 2. Wear the bulky stuff
slides.body: Heaviest shoes and jacket go on you, not in the bag. Free space for the price of feeling silly at security.

slides.headline: 3. Solid toiletries dodge the liquid rule
slides.body: Bar shampoo and solid deodorant aren't liquids. No baggie, no 100ml limit, no spills.

slides.headline: 4. One 'just in case' item, max
slides.body: You'll wear the same few things anyway. The 'what if' pile is what fills every oversized bag.

slides.headline: Survive a long layover
slides.body: 4 ways to make it painless

slides.headline: 1. Know if you can leave
slides.body: A 6-hour layover can be a mini city trip if visa rules allow. Check before you resign to the terminal.

slides.headline: 2. Find the quiet zones
slides.body: Prayer rooms, empty gates far from your own, upper floors. Every airport has calm corners if you walk.

slides.headline: 3. Charge everything, early
slides.body: Grab a socket the moment you land, not when your phone's at 5%. Outlets vanish near boarding time.

slides.headline: 4. A lounge can be worth it
slides.body: Some let you pay a flat entry. For a long wait, food, showers, and a real seat often beat the price.

slides.headline: Stay safe abroad
slides.body: 4 habits worth building

slides.headline: 1. Split your money
slides.body: Some cash in your wallet, some in your bag, a card elsewhere. One loss never leaves you stranded.

slides.headline: 2. Screenshot your key documents
slides.body: Passport, visa, hotel address, saved offline. If your phone dies or is stolen, you still have them.

slides.headline: 3. Trust the exit instinct
slides.body: If a place or person feels off, leave. You owe no politeness that overrides your gut abroad.

slides.headline: 4. Know two emergency numbers
slides.body: Local police and your embassy. Saved before you need them, not googled in a crisis.

slides.headline: Cut your electricity bill
slides.body: 4 changes that actually add up

slides.headline: 1. Standby is silently costing you
slides.body: Devices left on standby draw power all day. A switched power strip kills it in one flick.

slides.headline: 2. Fridge coils and door seals
slides.body: Dusty coils and weak seals make it work harder. A yearly clean and seal check cuts real cost.

slides.headline: 3. Wash cold, dry on the line
slides.body: Heating water is the big cost in laundry, and the dryer is a power hog. Cold + air-dry wins.

slides.headline: 4. The AC's sweet spot
slides.body: Each degree cooler jumps the bill. A moderate setting plus a fan feels the same for far less.

slides.headline: The only tools you need
slides.body: 5 that fix almost everything

slides.headline: 1. A drill/driver
slides.body: Screws in, screws out, drills holes. The one power tool that earns its space instantly.

slides.headline: 2. A claw hammer
slides.body: Drives nails and pulls them. Basic, but nothing else does the job when you need it.

slides.headline: 3. An adjustable spanner
slides.body: One tool, every nut and bolt size. Skip the whole set you'll never fully use.

slides.headline: 4. A spirit level (or your phone)
slides.body: Shelves and frames that are actually straight. Your phone has one built in if you're starting out.

slides.headline: Declutter without the dread
slides.body: 4 moves that make it easy

slides.headline: 1. One category, not one room
slides.body: All the books, or all the mugs — not 'the kitchen'. Seeing the full pile makes cutting obvious.

slides.headline: 2. The one-year rule
slides.body: Haven't used it in a year? You won't miss it. Sentimental items are the only exception.

slides.headline: 3. A 'maybe' box, sealed and dated
slides.body: Unsure? Box it, date it, store it. If you don't open it in 6 months, it goes unopened.

slides.headline: 4. Out the door same day
slides.body: A donate bag that lingers gets unpacked. Drop it off the day you fill it, or it comes back.

slides.headline: Plants you can't kill
slides.body: 4 that survive almost anything

slides.headline: 1. Snake plant
slides.body: Thrives on neglect and low light. Water it once a fortnight and forget it — it prefers that.

slides.headline: 2. Pothos
slides.body: Trails happily anywhere, tells you when it's thirsty by drooping, and perks right back up. Forgiving.

slides.headline: 3. ZZ plant
slides.body: Handles dark corners and missed waterings. The plant for a room with barely any light.

slides.headline: 4. The real killer is overwatering
slides.body: Most 'dead' plants drowned, not dried. When unsure, wait — dry roots recover, rotted ones don't.

slides.headline: A warmer home, no extra heating
slides.body: 4 fixes that cost almost nothing

slides.headline: 1. Block the draughts first
slides.body: A rolled towel at the door gap, sealed windows. You lose most heat through the cracks, not the walls.

slides.headline: 2. Let the sun in by day
slides.body: Open curtains on sunny windows, close them at dusk. Free heat in, then trapped before it escapes.

slides.headline: 3. Rugs on cold floors
slides.body: Bare floors pull warmth from the room and your feet. A rug is insulation you can walk on.

slides.headline: 4. Reverse your ceiling fan
slides.body: Most fans have a winter setting that pushes warm air back down. Warm air rises — send it back.

slides.headline: Upgrade a rental, deposit safe
slides.body: 4 changes you can undo

slides.headline: 1. Peel-and-stick, not paint
slides.body: Removable wallpaper and tiles transform a wall or splashback, then peel off clean when you leave.

slides.headline: 2. Swap the lighting, keep the old
slides.body: A warm bulb or a plug-in lamp changes a room instantly. Box the original fitting to reinstall later.

slides.headline: 3. Command hooks over nails
slides.body: Hang art and shelves with no holes. Your deposit survives, your walls still look lived-in.

slides.headline: 4. Layer with textiles
slides.body: Rugs, cushions, throws add warmth and colour landlords never provide — and they come with you.
